Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Environment › Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment › Air pollution — GRAP, CAQM
CA Topic / Headline: Delhi winter pollution curbs kick in from Nov 1: non-Delhi non-BS-VI vehicles barred, no fuel without valid PUC; CPCB orders closure of NCR units that have not ordered APCDs within five days; CAQM PM limit 50 mg/Nm3 for 17 highly polluting categories.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• CAQM PM emission limit: 50 mg/Nm3 for 17 highly polluting industry categories, applicable from October 1.
• APCDs are filtration and emission-control systems fitted to industrial exhaust stacks; bag filters are one type.
• Delhi curbs: non-Delhi non-BS-VI vehicles barred from Nov 1 to Jan 31; no fuel without valid PUC certificate.
• Rain pulled Delhi average AQI down to 60 on Friday, per the IITM-maintained network.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] Several NCR units had not ordered new APCDs or obtained adequacy assessment reports, prompting CPCB closure directions.
• [Intro data] CPCB letter of October 30 asked Delhi PCC and Haryana, U.P., Rajasthan boards to issue show-cause notices.
• [Way forward] Pair vehicle curbs with continuous stack monitoring, time-bound APCD retrofits and region-wide enforcement across NCR States.
• [Counterpoint] Seasonal bans hurt gig workers and border traffic while year-round sources keep emitting.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Science & Technology › IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology, biotechnology, intellectual property rights › NavIC — NVS series
CA Topic / Headline: GSLV-F18 places NVS-03 in orbit (apogee 38,080 km vs planned 37,247 km), restoring NavIC to its minimum four-satellite configuration; ISRO flew it with pyro valves pre-opened after the NVS-02 failure.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• NVS-03 launched on GSLV-F18 from Sriharikota on October 30.
• NavIC needs at least four satellites for standalone positioning; NVS-03 restored that minimum.
• NVS-03 has a 12-year mission life and adds the L1 band (V&R).
• Last atomic clock aboard IRNSS-1F stopped working in March.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] NVS-02 (2025) failed because the drive signal did not reach the oxidiser pyro valve.
• [Issue] Indigenous clocks face procurement challenges; ISRO proposes up to five clocks per satellite.
• [Way forward] Launch NVS-04 and NVS-05 quickly, mandate NavIC chipsets and build clock supply chains.
• [Intro data] Original IRNSS satellites were launched between 2013 and 2018.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Internal Security › Communication networks, media and social networking, cyber security, money-laundering › Content blocking — Sec 69A, 79(3)(b), IT Rules
CA Topic / Headline: MeitY advisories of October 8 and 10 amid anti-CEC protests drive a wave of post and account blocking on Meta and X; amended IT Rules cut takedown time to three hours from 36; users face 60-90 day grievance delays.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Section 69A, IT Act, 2000: Centre may block online content on sovereignty, security, public order grounds.
• Section 79(3)(b): safe-harbour can lapse if an intermediary fails to act on lawful notice.
• Rule 3(1)(d), IT Rules 2021: takedown within three hours of court order or authorised intimation.
• Grievance Appellate Committee hears appeals against platform grievance officers’ decisions.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] Platform-level removals under community standards leave users without constitutional-court remedy, per advocate Rishav Ranjan.
• [Intro data] Delhi Police issued about 300 takedown requests in three months, most acted upon (V&R).
• [Way forward] Publish reasoned orders, add notice and hearing, and set time-bound GAC review.
• [Counterpoint] Rapid removal limits deepfakes and incitement during volatile protests.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Economy › Infrastructure: energy, ports, roads, airports, railways › Ethanol blending — E20, E100, flex-fuel
CA Topic / Headline: MoRTH amends Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 to include E100 alongside E85, paving way for flex-fuel vehicle homologation; existing vehicles need not switch; India hit E20 in 2025, five years early.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• E100 is fuel with 100% ethanol; usable only in vehicles designed for it.
• India achieved E20 in 2025, five years ahead of the 2030 deadline under National Policy on Biofuels, 2018.
• From April 2026, all BS-VI vehicles must meet E20 emission standards.
• Homologation is official certification by agencies such as ARAI before type approval.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] Ethanol’s lower energy density lowers mileage; government estimates about 5% decline.
• [Issue] Large-scale ethanol needs land and water and competes with food crops.
• [Counterpoint] Experts warn blending distracts from electrification, a clearer path to deep emission cuts.
• [Way forward] Diversify to second-generation feedstock, track lifecycle emissions and build flex-fuel dispensing.

CA Topic / Headline: SC to review AITUC challenge to Section 2(p) of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 ‘industry’ definition: Article 14 and excessive delegation; Jai Bir Singh (Aug 2026) kept the 1978 triple test for pending 1947-Act disputes.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Section 2(p) of the IR Code, 2020 defines ‘industry’ as systematic activity through employer-worker cooperation for producing or supplying goods or services.
• The Code consolidates the Trade Unions Act 1926, Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act 1946 and Industrial Disputes Act 1947.
• Exclusions: charitable, social or philanthropic institutions, sovereign functions, domestic services and activities notified by the Centre.
• Bangalore Water Supply v. A. Rajappa (1978) set the “triple test” focusing on nature of activity, not employer identity.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] Jai Bir Singh (August 2026): the 1978 test still governs pending 1947-Act disputes, but Section 2(p) must be read independently.
• [Issue] Petition says exclusions depend on who runs an establishment, violating Article 14, and the Centre’s power to add exclusions is unguided.
• [Issue] Workers in excluded establishments lose Code protections on retrenchment, lay-off, closure and conciliation.
• [Way forward] Retain the functional test with objective notified exclusions to protect workers while avoiding over-breadth.

Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Article 168: six States have Councils — Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.
• Article 169: Parliament, by ordinary law, may create or abolish a Council if the Assembly passes a resolution by two-thirds majority.
• Article 171: at most one-third of Assembly strength, minimum 40; one-third elected by local bodies and one-third by MLAs; one-sixth nominated.
• Article 172: not subject to dissolution; members’ term six years, one-third retiring every two years.
• Council can delay an Assembly-passed bill for a maximum of four months.

• [Intro data] 1935 Act introduced bicameral legislatures in six provinces; Constituent Assembly debated Councils as a check on hasty legislation.
• [Counterpoint] Critics call Councils an unnecessary exchequer burden and object that key aspects are left to ordinary law; supporters cite their revising role.

• Court said eradication of bonded labour is a continuing obligation; release is not the end of the State’s duty.
• Centre to lay down a uniform procedure for financial assistance within seven days of release.
• Centre to consider revising the rehabilitation scheme within three months and give “subsistence support” for delays.
• Revised SOP framed on 14 May: States/UTs to implement within six months; supplementary guidelines with NHRC within three months.
• Complaints to be verified ordinarily within 24 hours; release certificate to follow inquiry.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] Constitutional prohibition and statutory measures cannot remain “mere assurances on paper”; identification, release and rehabilitation are interconnected stages.
• [Issue] Delays in financial assistance and institutional gaps in identifying and rehabilitating rescued workers keep survivors vulnerable.
• [Way forward] 24-hour verification, time-bound release certificates, funds within seven days and NHRC-guided guidelines.
• [Ethics] Dignity of life requires rehabilitation, not merely rescue.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Economy › Infrastructure: energy, ports, roads, airports, railways › Civil aviation — Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, airfares
CA Topic / Headline: Rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 (notified 31 October) let the Centre issue written directions on airfares in ‘extraordinary situations’; airlines must publish tariffs; no fare caps.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Rules notified on e-Gazette on 31 October under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024.
• Centre can issue written directions to airlines on airfares in the public interest during “extraordinary situations” (undefined).
• Airlines must submit tariffs to the DGCA and publish them on websites or DGCA-specified platforms.
• Fares shown must give the total payable with breakdown of base fare, taxes, fees, cancellation charges and refund conditions.
• Air Transport Circular 2 of 2010 (19 November 2010) already required fare data submission; now codified.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] Rules do not define “extraordinary situations”; government earlier imposed fare bands in COVID-19 and after IndiGo’s December disruption (nearly 5,000 flights cancelled).
• [Issue] Rules follow a PIL by social activist S. Laxminarayan seeking binding norms against arbitrary airfares and ancillary charges in festive seasons and emergencies.
• [Intro data] Government retains position that airfares are market-driven since the Air Corporations Act was repealed in March 1994.
• [Way forward] Transparent price monitoring with narrow, defined triggers balances consumer protection and airline viability.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Science & Technology › IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology, biotechnology, intellectual property rights › Data protection — DPDP Act, AI training
CA Topic / Headline: Op-ed: DPDP Act (2023; Rules notified November 2025) does not cover publicly available or inferred data, creates no sensitive-data category and is silent on AI training; consent provisions apply only from 2027 and users have no right to object.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• DPDP Act passed in 2023; DPDP Rules notified in November 2025; implementation is phased.
• Substantive provisions take full effect in May 2027; consent and safety provisions effective only in 2027.
• Right to privacy was upheld by the Supreme Court in 2017.
• IT Act, 2000 and 2011 Rules covered ‘sensitive personal data’, with criminal penalty capped at three years’ imprisonment or ₹5 lakh fine.
• DPDP right to erasure applies only to data given with consent; research, archival and statistical processing is exempt.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] DPDP Act excludes publicly available data and inferred data (emotions, mobility, behaviour), and buckets all personal data together with no sensitive category.
• [Issue] AI models can regurgitate training data; “anonymised” datasets can be used to extract personal details and profile individuals.
• [Way forward] Apply the Act to AI training data, give a right to object, strengthen erasure, clarify the research exemption and create a sensitive-data category.
• [Counterpoint] Indiscriminate regulation risks inhibiting innovation; Meta allows EU users an AI-training opt-out but Indians have none.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › India and its neighbourhood relations › Brahmaputra — Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, China mega-dam
CA Topic / Headline: Editorial: 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) is a strategic buffer against China’s 60-GW Tibet mega-dam, but top-down approach and UAPA cases against activists fuel Adi land fears; urges respect for land rights.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• SUMP planned at 11.2 GW in Upper Siang, Arunachal Pradesh, as a buffer against China’s 60-GW dam on the Yarlung Tsangpo.
• The Yarlung Tsangpo becomes the Brahmaputra in India; the Tibet dam has five cascading stations over a 2,000-metre fall.
• China has agreed only to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies.
• Planners considered keeping the SUMP reservoir at 70% to absorb surges.
• Protests also exist against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project.
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Issue] Security forces guard survey teams and the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act is used against activists, validating fears of land grab.
• [Issue] China declines to share engineering details; downstream flow is mostly monsoon and tributary-fed, limiting Chinese control but not near-border risks.
• [Way forward] Diplomacy for data-sharing, plus compliance with all laws and protections, and consent of Adi communities.
• [Ethics] The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

[Syllabus base – Air pollution — GRAP, CAQM] (V&R: Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), Mechanism, Stages, Challenges)
• GRAP was framed after Supreme Court directions in M.C. Mehta vs Union of India (2016) to tackle air pollution in Delhi-NCR.

• GRAP is preventive: IMD and IITM/SAFAR forecasts trigger stages before pollution peaks.

[Syllabus base – Public Accounts Committee — CAG reports] (V&R: Public Accounts Committee, History, Members, Purpose; Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), Article, Reports)
• It has 22 members: 15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha; the term is one year and Ministers cannot be members.
